fiscal_year_note: Calendar fiscal year. PDF filename year matches actual fiscal year.
reporting_unit_warning: Block reports segment and tax figures in THOUSANDS, unlike most peers in this set which report in millions. Mis-scaling by 1000x is the single most likely extraction error for this filing.

accrued_amount.note: No single aggregate legal accrual figure captured in this pass.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Block explicitly states a reasonably possible loss that could be material, but that it cannot estimate the amount or range.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: It is reasonably possible that the Company will incur a loss in connection with these federal securities and derivative matters, and the loss could be material; however, the Company cannot estimate the amount of loss or range of loss at this time.

individual_matters.note: A separate state-attorneys-general matter was noted during review as carrying a probable loss, but its verbatim language and amount were not captured in this pass and are therefore NOT asserted as ground truth.

legal_contingencies.why_hard: This is one of the few filings in the set with an explicit, unambiguous 'reasonably possible ... could be material ... cannot estimate' construction tied to a named matter category — the correct answer is 'disclosed but not quantifiable', not a number.

segment_reporting.profit_measure_note: Block's segment profitability measure is GROSS PROFIT, not operating income. There is no segment operating income disclosure.

reconciling_items.label: Corporate and Other
reconciling_items.note: Not a reportable segment — a residual/reconciling column presented alongside the two reportable segments.

traps: Figures are in THOUSANDS, not millions.
Segment profit measure is gross profit, not operating income — an extractor looking for 'segment operating income' will find nothing and may wrongly report 'not disclosed'.
'Corporate and Other' is a reconciling column, not a third reportable segment.
Bitcoin ecosystem revenue ($8.5B of $24.2B total) is gross bitcoin sales with a near-equal cost of revenue, so revenue-based segment weighting is highly misleading vs gross profit.
A goodwill-by-segment table (lines 1763-1770) uses the same Cash App / Square / Corporate and Other column headers and can be mistaken for the segment results table.

income_taxes.statutory_rate_print_note: The FY2025 reconciliation table literally prints '21.2 %' on the 'Tax at federal statutory rate' line. The true US federal statutory rate is 21.0%; the 21.2% is the filing's own computed percentage on that row. Ground truth records BOTH: statutory_federal_rate_percent = 21.0, as-printed = 21.2.
income_taxes.income_before_income_taxes_note: Implied as 385,701 / 0.228; the reconciliation table does not print pretax income. Consistent with 357,813 / 1,691,671 = 21.15% ≈ the printed 21.2%.
income_taxes.reconciliation_presentation: dollars and percent, FY2025 column only in this block

unrecognized_tax_benefits.unit_note: This particular sentence is stated in millions even though the tables are in thousands.
unrecognized_tax_benefits.remainder_treatment: The remainder would result in a corresponding adjustment to the valuation allowance.
unrecognized_tax_benefits.verbatim_quote: As of December 31, 2025, the Company had unrecognized tax benefits of $626.8 million, of which $69.1 million would impact the annual effective tax rate if recognized and the remainder of which would result in a corresponding adjustment to the valuation allowance.

traps: The printed 21.2% statutory rate contradicts the 21.0% US federal rate — an extractor that 'corrects' it loses the as-filed value, one that copies it may wrongly report the statutory rate as 21.2%.
Only $69.1M of the $626.8M UTB would affect the ETR (11%) because most is offset by valuation allowance — reporting $626.8M as the ETR-affecting figure is a 9x error.
Tax tables are in thousands but the UTB narrative is in millions, within the same note.
